jobs.title: CDC Global Immunization and Polio Eradication Fellowship at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 12/06/2026 Description*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.CDC Office and Location: A research opportunity is currently available at The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in Atlanta, Georgia. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is one of the major operation components of the Department of Health and Human Services. CDC protects America from health, safety and security threats, both foreign and in the U.S. Whether diseases start at home or abroad, are chronic or acute, curable or preventable, human error or deliberate attack, CDC fights disease and supports communities and citizens to do the same. CDC increases the health security of our nation. As the nation’s health protection agency, CDC saves lives and protects people from health threats. To accomplish its mission, CDC conducts important science and provides health information that protects our nation against expensive and dangerous health threats, and responds when these arise.Research Project: You will participate in a mentored fellowship with CDC’s Global Immunization Division (GID) focused on the scientific and public health approaches associated with global polio eradication. Through interactions with CDC technical personnel, you will learn about strategic, analytical, epidemiologic, and communication approaches used in polio eradication, including preparedness for and response to poliovirus outbreaks. As learning opportunities arise, you may also gain exposure to broader emergency preparedness and response approaches, including those used within CDC’s Emergency Operations Center (EOC) and Incident Management Structure (IMS).You will learn how technical and regional teams collaborate on global polio eradication activities; gain experience analyzing and synthesizing epidemiologic, programmatic, and outbreak-related information; and develop an understanding of how briefings, updates, and other informational materials communicate scientific findings. You will also strengthen collaboration skills through interactions across CDC programs and gain insight into partnerships involving Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) organizations and U.S. Government counterparts.You may gain mentored research experience related to outbreak preparedness and response, including analysis of outbreak and response data, examination of response-planning approaches, and research on guidance documents and information systems associated with outbreak readiness. Additional learning opportunities may include gaining familiarity with analytical tools and resources used to assess preparedness and observing or participating in educational and research activities related to polio outbreak response alongside experienced epidemiologists and other technical personnel.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will strengthen skills in applied epidemiology, data analysis, global immunization program approaches, outbreak preparedness and response research, and scientific communication. You will gain experience analyzing and interpreting epidemiologic and outbreak-related information, learn how scientific evidence informs public health practice, and develop an understanding of the epidemiologic, analytical, and collaborative approaches used in global polio eradication and emergency preparedness.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Monica Fleming (njl9@cdc.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research please contact the mentor(s).Anticipated Appointment Start Date: January 11, 2027. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be between January 2027 - September 2027, but may be renewed upon recommendation of CDC and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is full time.Participant Stipend: Stipend rates may vary based on numerous factors, including opportunity, location, education, and experience. If you are interviewed, you can inquire about the exact stipend rate at that time and if selected, your appointment offer will include the monthly stipend rate.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens, Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR), and foreign nationals. Non-U.S. citizen applicants should refer to the Guidelines for Non-U.S. Citizens Details page of the program website for information about the valid immigration statuses that are acceptable for program participation.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and CDC. Participants do not become employees of CDC, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the hosting facility, including but not limited to, poliovirus requirements (e.g. immunization, testing prior to laboratory access).Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process please email CDCrpp@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should have received or be currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in one of the relevant fields. Preferred skills:Graduate-level training or equivalent experience in public health, epidemiology, global health, immunization, infectious diseases, emergency management, or a related field.Experience analyzing epidemiologic, surveillance, programmatic, or operational data.Familiarity with infectious disease prevention, vaccination programs, outbreak response, emergency preparedness, or public health programs.Ability to synthesize complex information into concise briefings, reports, presentations, dashboards, and other decision-support items.Strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to explain technical information to diverse audiences.Ability to collaborate with domestic and international partners, manage multiple priorities, act independently, and adapt to evolving program needs.Stipend$5,439.25 MonthlyPoint of ContactRachelEligibility RequirementsDegree: Bachelor's Degree or Master's Degree received within the last 60 months or currently pursuing.

jobs.description: Employer: Vizient, Inc. Expires: 12/07/2026 Vizient Intern Program Overview: This program is designed to foster a beneficial relationship and provide growth opportunities for Vizient, our employees, and collegiate students. Since 2000, our summer intern program has provided college undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students with practical experience that exposes them to multiple aspects of a career field and the healthcare industry. This full-time, paid intern program offers an opportunity to accelerate academic learning, apply classroom knowledge, and introduce students to a professional setting. About the team and role The Research Analytics & Insights (RAIN) team uses Vizient data and research methods to generate evidence and insights that help healthcare organizations understand performance, quality outcomes, and emerging industry questions. The team supports internal research priorities and member-focused analyses by combining background research, thoughtful study design, data analysis, and clear communication of findings. The intern will receive hands-on training in the Vizient Clinical Data Base (CDB) and contribute to a defined healthcare analytics project. Working with the RAIN team, the intern will develop an analytic question, identify relevant data and literature, conduct and interpret analyses, and translate findings into a concise final presentation or research deliverable. Contribute to a defined research or analytics project addressing a RAIN team priority or client-relevant healthcare question. Conduct focused literature and background research, refine analytic questions, and identify appropriate measures and datasets. Perform data extraction, validation, descriptive analysis, and interpretation to identify meaningful trends and insights. Collaborate with RAIN colleagues and cross-functional partners to review methods, findings, and implications. Develop clear documentation, visualizations, and a final presentation or written research deliverable for technical and nontechnical audiences. Support updates to internal SharePoint content and team knowledge resources, as needed. What You’ll Learn How healthcare data and research are used to evaluate quality, utilization, outcomes, and performance. Practical use of administrative claims-based data and a structured workflow for moving from a research question to an analytic result. Methods for literature review, measure definition, data validation, interpretation, and responsible communication of findings. How research and analytics teams partner with internal stakeholders and healthcare organizations. Professional skills in project planning, data storytelling, presentation development, and stakeholder communication. Qualifications Currently pursuing a master’s or doctoral degree in health services research, public health, epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, health informatics, healthcare administration, or a related quantitative field; an undergraduate degree must be completed before the internship begins. jobs.title: 2027 Department of Transportation Summer Internship Program at Federal Highway Administration
jobs.description: Employer: Federal Highway Administration Expires: 12/08/2026 Don't Delay - Start Your Career Today with FHWA!The United States Department of Transportation (in collaboration with GMG Management Consulting, Inc.) is recruiting for its 2027 Department of Transportation Summer Internship (DOTSI) Program. Learn more about the DOTSI Program by visiting https://gmgedu.com/ (open to U.S. Citizens). During the 10-week program, those selected at the undergraduate level receive a $5,500 stipend while those individuals in graduate or law school receive $7,500. Each person chosen for the program also receives round-trip travel to their assigned summer office and complimentary housing at that location if they reside 50 miles or more from their placement site. The DOTSI Program application deadline is 01/31/2027, but submit your application early for optimal consideration.The mission of the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) is to advance safety, move people and goods efficiently, and build resilient infrastructure. USDOT's key values and priorities include safety first, affordability and efficiency, and accelerating innovation.GMG Management Consulting's mission centers on building and broadening the future workforce of the nation's transportation and public infrastructure sectors. Through its administration of DOTSI, GMG works to bridge higher education with government service: providing undergraduate, graduate, and law students with structured, hands-on experience across Federal transportation agencies.Click here to learn more about DOTSI and apply!===What is DOTSI?For over two decades, DOTSI has provided students with valuable summer employment opportunities designed to kickstart their careers in the transportation sector. As a premier workforce development program, DOTSI encourages students to enter public service by offering hands-on experience across various government functions. Participants gain a behind-the-scenes look at federal operations and decision-making processes, giving them the practical knowledge needed to eventually fill mission-critical roles within the industry.Beyond day-to-day work experience, DOTSI is specifically designed to support your long-term career advancement through dedicated mentorship and professional networking. As a participant, you will be paired with experienced DOT mentors who will guide you throughout the program, helping you build lasting professional connections and deeply understand your potential career pathways. Ultimately, the program fosters a highly qualified talent pool, making it easier for you to confidently step into a rewarding future in public service and the transportation field.---What is the length of the summer internship?The DOTSI program is a 10-week summer experience that provides undergraduate, graduate, and law students with the opportunity to sharpen their research, writing, and presentation skills through hands-on work. Beyond your daily assignments, you will participate in a variety of enriching activities tailored to your role, including field trips to national transportation facilities, industry conferences, skill-building workshops, and high-level decision-making meetings.---What are some of the learning outcomes of the program?Through the DOTSI Program, interns will achieve key learning outcomes designed to build highly transferable professional skills. Participants will sharpen their analytical research, professional writing, and public presentation abilities by executing hands-on, mission-critical assignments within a Federal agency. Additionally, students will develop strong cross-functional collaboration and networking skills by working alongside multidisciplinary teams and experienced DOT mentors, ultimately gaining practical insights into complex policy and decision-making processes that will serve them in any future career.---What accommodations and compensation do summer interns receive?DOTSI interns receive a competitive stipend of $5,500 for undergraduate students and $7,500 for graduate and law students (stipends are subject to applicable taxes). Additionally, to ensure the program is accessible, interns who live 50 or more miles away from their assigned summer office will receive fully furnished housing and paid roundtrip travel to and from their placement location.---I want to apply! What does the application process look like?To be considered for the DOTSI Program, you must complete the application and submit all required documents by Saturday, January 31, 2027. The selection process begins in late February, and all applicants will be notified of their status via e-mail no later than May 1st. If you are selected, you must reply by e-mail to accept the offer within a specified number of business days, otherwise the offer will be extended to another qualified applicant.To apply, you must meet the following requirements and submit the corresponding materials:Be a U.S. Citizen: As this is a federal internship with the U.S. Department of Transportation, U.S. citizenship is legally required.Be Enrolled in a Degree Program: You must be enrolled in a degree-granting program at an accredited U.S. institution during the Spring 2027 semester, with continued enrollment planned for Fall 2027. You must also maintain a GPA of 3.0 or higher.Complete the Application: Ensure the application is fully completed and confirm your availability to participate for the entire 10-week summer program.Submit Academic Transcripts: Provide a copy of your most recent transcript or grade report. (File naming convention: First Name_Last Name_Transcript_Year).Attach a Resume: Provide a one-page resume highlighting your work experience (paid and unpaid), volunteer roles, awards, leadership experience, and extracurricular activities. (File naming convention: First Name_Last Name_Resume).Provide One Letter of Reference: Submit a current written recommendation from a department chair, professor, academic advisor, or employer. (File naming convention: First Name_Last Name_Reference).Include a Writing Sample: Submit a writing sample tailored to your academic level. Undergraduates must submit a one-page, double-spaced essay (12-point font minimum) on their transportation interests and career goals; master’s students must submit a sample, up to two pages, detailing their academic and career goals related to transportation; and law students must submit a legal writing sample up to five pages. (File naming convention: First Name_Last Name_Writing Sample).Please note: Priority will be given to candidates with GPAs of 3.0 or higher (major and/or cumulative).Click here to learn more about DOTSI and apply!===The DOT "Modes"DOTSI Program participants may work in any of DOT's 11 operating administrations (OAs).The OAs are more commonly referred to as "modes" of transportation:Office of the Secretary of Transportation: OST relies on a dedicated workforce of approximately 800 to 1,000 employees to serve as the principal policy-making and oversight body for the entire U.S. Department of Transportation. OST coordinates national transportation strategies, manages major infrastructure grant programs, and ensures all operating administrations work cohesively to deliver a safe, equitable, and modern transportation system.Federal Aviation Administration: FAA employs approximately 40,000 to 45,000 dedicated professionals who work tirelessly to regulate civil aviation and manage the nation's complex air traffic control system. The agency collaborates with the airline industry and airports to enforce strict aviation regulations and ensure the safest, most efficient aerospace system in the world.Federal Highway Administration: FHWA utilizes its workforce of roughly 2,300 to 2,800 employees to partner with state and local governments in designing, building, and maintaining the nation's highway and bridge infrastructure. The agency is dedicated to delivering a world-class system that ensures safe, reliable travel across interstate networks, national forests, Indian reservations, and other public lands.Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration: FMCSA relies on a dedicated team of 1,000 to 1,200 employees to reduce crashes, injuries, and fatalities involving large trucks and buses on our national highways. The agency collaborates with federal, state, and local enforcement groups to implement strict commercial vehicle regulations and promote rigorous safety standards across the motor carrier industry.Federal Railroad Administration: FRA leverages its team of 950 to 1,100 personnel to promote and enforce safety regulations across America's expansive freight and passenger rail networks. The agency works diligently to ensure that tracks, equipment, and operations remain in safe, working condition to facilitate the reliable movement of people and goods nationwide.Maritime Administration: MARAD operates with a workforce of about 700 to 850 employees who are committed to fostering the development and maintenance of a robust United States merchant marine and maritime industry. The agency actively supports waterborne transportation by improving port infrastructure, ensuring ship safety, and advancing seamless integration with other land-based transportation networks. Additionally, MARAD oversees the United States Merchant Marine Academy in Kings Point (New York), which educates and trains future leaders of the nation's maritime services.National Highway Traffic Safety Administration: NHTSA employs roughly 550 to 750 professionals dedicated to saving lives, preventing injuries, and reducing vehicle-related crashes on U.S. roadways. The agency achieves this critical mission by setting rigorous vehicle performance standards, enforcing recalls for safety defects, and educating the public on safe driving behaviors.Federal Transit Administration: FTA relies on between 500 and 600 staff members who work closely with state and local transit providers to fund and support comprehensive public transportation systems, including buses, subways, and ferries. The agency prioritizes improving mobility, promoting environmental sustainability, and ensuring equitable access to safe and reliable transit options for all communities.Office of Inspector General: OIG utilizes a specialized staff of 350 to 425 auditors and investigators to provide independent, objective oversight of the Department of Transportation's programs and operations. The agency is fundamentally committed to enhancing program efficiency and integrity by actively detecting and preventing fraud, waste, and abuse across all transportation sectors.Great Lakes-St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation: GLS operates with a focused team of 120 to 145 employees responsible for the safe, efficient, and reliable operation of the U.S. portion of the St. Lawrence Seaway. The agency works in tandem with its Canadian counterparts to manage essential lock facilities, promote maritime commerce, and ensure environmental stewardship along this vital international shipping corridor.Click here to learn more about DOTSI and apply!===Get in Touch with Our Team!We want to make sure you have everything you need to submit a successful application! Reach out to DOSTI staff at gmg-dotsi@gmgedu.com and we will be happy to assist you!Click here to learn more about DOTSI and apply!===Please also share with others who may be interested!

jobs.title: AmeriCorps Summer Teaching Fellow at SSC Learning Network
jobs.description: Employer: SSC Learning Network Expires: 12/08/2026 About Breakthrough Silicon ValleyBreakthrough Silicon Valley launches talented students who have been historically excluded from higher education on the path to college, and inspires high school and college students to become the next generation of leaders, advocates, and educators. BTSV’s six -year college access and success program, which supports students from 7th grade to first year of college, has proven to be effective in preparing these students for college: a stunning 99% of BTSV graduates attend college immediately after high school. BTSV’s tuition-free program provides year-round out-of-school time academic support, advising, and advocacy for a diverse group of talented students, most of whom come from under-resourced communities and will be the first generation in their family to go to college. Through our students-teaching-students model, BTSV also provides a consummate professional development experience providing talented high school and college students the opportunity to understand the K-12 system and the drivers of educational inequities, and to design and teach classes under the direction of seasoned educators. Located in San Jose, California, Breakthrough Silicon Valley is an affiliate of The Breakthrough Collaborative, a leading national service organization that acts as the national voice for 25 Breakthrough sites across the country. About the Summer Teaching FellowshipYour Impact: Our summer program could not be what it is every year without the dedicated service of our Teaching Fellows. You won’t just be a teacher. You’ll be a mentor and a role model to your students. You will witness how your leadership helps your students grow personally and progress academically in just a few weeks. What does a typical summer look like?Pre-Service Orientation TrainingYour journey begins with an immersive Pre-Service Orientation. During the first few days, you'll dive into the essentials of lesson planning, instructional strategies, and classroom management techniques. Alongside other AmeriCorps Teaching Fellows, you’ll build connections, form lasting friendships, and become familiar with Breakthrough's vibrant culture and mission. During this time, you’ll meet your Instructional Coach, a seasoned educator in your subject area, who will mentor you throughout the summer. This guidance will set the foundation for your success in the classroom.The Summer Program ExperienceTeaching Fellows are responsible for delivering engaging instruction in core academic subjects such as reading, writing, math, and science, as well as leading elective classes that inspire and motivate middle school students. In addition, Fellows serve as Crew Leaders, fostering community and building relationships through daily crew time by planning and facilitating icebreakers, energizers, and team-building activities. Fellows serve closely with an Instructional Coach, participating in regular meetings to strengthen their teaching and leadership skills while incorporating feedback to support continuous professional growth as educators.But it's not all work! Breakthrough’s summer is packed with joy-filled traditions like college campus visits, the summer talent show, Spirit Week, field days, and the Breakthrough Olympics. You’ll not only help students learn but also build a community of fun, encouragement, and support that will leave a lasting impact.Wrap-Up Week and Reflecting on Your ImpactAt the end of the summer, you'll celebrate the achievements of your students and reflect on the incredible growth you’ve witnessed in them—and yourself. Wrap-Up Week provides time to document these experiences and share your insights. It also offers career-building opportunities through panels featuring local professionals in fields like counseling, educational technology, higher education, and youth development. These sessions will help you envision your next steps as a future leader in education or beyond.This journey will not only give you hands-on teaching experience but also prepare you for a meaningful career, surrounded by a community that celebrates growth, learning, and the joy of teaching. Mentorship and GuidanceYou will serve under the mentorship of an experienced Instructional Coach, who will review your lesson plans, provide daily feedback, and train you in effective teaching strategies, classroom management, and student assessment techniques. Teaching Fellows will receive their Performance Review at the conclusion of their service. The final performance review will also include:Whether the member has completed the required number of hoursWhether the member has satisfactorily completed assignmentsWhether the member has met other performance criteria that were clearly communicated at the beginning of the term of service and in the member's position description.Ideal CandidateThis position is perfect for you if:You are passionate about serving with middle- and high-school students.You are eager to tackle a steep learning curve with enthusiasm and an open mind.You pride yourself on your organizational skills and attention to detail.You are looking to start a career in education, social justice, or public service.You enjoy laughter and having fun while making a difference.You can commit to 300+ hours of service from June 14 to August 6, 2027, serving full-time hours throughout the program.Embark on a summer journey that will not only enrich your professional skills but also leave a lasting impact on the lives of young students. Join us as a Teaching Fellow and make this summer unforgettable! Training and Professional DevelopmentBTSV wants you to learn and grow as much as your students will. At the start of your service, you will receive a comprehensive orientation to your new team, to BTSV, our program, and your role. Throughout the summer program you will serve with your colleagues, BTSV Staff, and with the expert guidance of an Instructional Coach, an experienced educator who will provide training, coaching, observation, feedback, encouragement, and support. Members will receive formal and structured feedback via performance reviews. Note, training hours will not exceed 20% of total service hours. Requirements“Breakthrough Spirit”: You’re a collaborative team player who is committed to excellence and is open-minded. You demonstrate a growth mindset, think creatively to solve problems, and serve with a sense of humor and humility.Commitment to Breakthrough Silicon Valley’s mission and goals as well as a passion for educational equity.Have a commitment to community service and the ability to serve the full service term. (300+ hrs of service, full-time from June 14 to August 6, 2027)Recent college graduate, or currently enrolled in college or high school.At least 17 years old at the start of the service period (June 14, 2027).Candidates 18 years of age or older must pass a National Service Criminal History Check.US citizen, US national, or lawful permanent resident of the United States.Access to reliable transportation to our summer program sites via personal vehicle, public transit, or other means.Spanish or Vietnamese language skills are a plus, but not required. Compensation & BenefitsAmeriCorps positions are volunteer roles which carry a living allowance. BTSV’s AmeriCorps Members will receive:$5,294 living allowance (pre-tax) paid semi-monthly over the service period.Summer Teaching Fellows who complete their AmeriCorps service are eligible for a $1,565.08 education award via the Segal AmeriCorps Education Award. This can be used for continuing education or to repay certain student loans.Student loan forbearance, if eligible. Location(s)BTSV maintains two offices in San Jose and our Summer Program sites will be co-located or nearby to these offices:Bridges Academy: 1702 McLaughlin Ave, San Jose, CA 95122Herbert Hoover Middle School: 1635 Park Ave, San Jose, CA 95126 Teaching Fellows are required to serve full-time in person. This is not a remote position. Application ProcessApply online at http://breakthroughsv.org/becomeateachingfellow. We will review applications on a rolling basis.

jobs.title: Environmental Education Intern at Prescott Farm Environmental Education Center
jobs.description: Employer: Prescott Farm Environmental Education Center Expires: 12/09/2026 Job Title: Environmental Education InternReports To: Camp & School-Age Programs DirectorEffective Dates Option #1: mid-February – mid-June (exact dates agreed upon with Camp & School-Age Programs Director)Effective Dates Option #2: mid-February – late-August (exact dates agreed upon with Camp & School-Age Programs Director)Working Hours: approximately 10-20 hours/week during all weeks EXCEPT 36-40 hours/week only during camp weeks (camp weeks are February 22-26, April 26-30, and June 21-August 27) – interns will also work Saturdays in MarchSalary Level: $16/hourEmployment Status: Temporary, Hourly, Non-exempt Internship Summary:Prescott Farm Environmental Education Center seeks enthusiastic, positive, and kind interns to lead education programs with the guidance of our education team. We will provide training on how to teach our programs so that interns can lead field trips at Prescott Farm and assist in teaching programs at our partnering schools with our Environmental Educators. Interns will also develop and implement programs for campers which they will lead during Winter Camp (February 22-26), Spring Camp (April 26-30), and/or Summer Camp (June 21-August 27). We ask that interns complete at least one project of their choice during their term that will support our mission, examples of some project ideas can be found below but should be based on the intern’s interests and organization’s needs. Interns must also present some sort of culmination of their internship experience and projects to the staff of Prescott Farm. The exact details of the presentation can be worked out depending on the projects they complete and the intern’s interests.During camp, interns work 36-40 hours Monday through Friday, typically 8:30am to 4:30pm, with the exception of 3-4 shifts of extended care coverage per week (the before care shift starts at 7:45am and the after care shift ends at 5pm). Interns will be paired with another intern or camp instructor and together they will be assigned a group of up to 12 campers. They are responsible for daily supervision and instruction of their campers as well as the larger camp community ages 5-14. Interns will develop programs and activities for campers and lead them through their day. Activity topics may include but are not limited to environmental science, plant and animal ID, natural exploration of the forest, fields, and wetlands, fire-making, cooking, gardening, shelter-building, and teambuilding. We ask interns to prioritize teaching hands-on, outdoor programs that encourage exploration of and care for our natural environment and wildlife.This position is in-person in Laconia, NH and interns must have access to a personal vehicle in order to commute to and from work (there is no reliable public transportation in the area). Housing is not provided. Responsibilities:Lead educational experiences on- and off-site to children ages 5-18 and occasionally adultsComplete at least one project that supports Prescott Farm’s mission (examples below)Maintain safe, kind, proactive, and inclusive behavior management strategies with childrenArrive on time for all scheduled days and stay for the entire duration of your scheduled timeCommunicate any anticipated and emergency time off in a timely manner with the Camp DirectorUse the Prescott Farm 2-way radios to communicate with other staff members during the dayShare in maintenance of program equipmentOccasionally assist with preschool age students with preschool teachers presentOther duties as assignedAdditional Responsibilities During Camp:Supervise campers and maintain safe practices, upholding all WildQuest Camp policies Develop and lead programs and activities for campers on a variety of science and nature topics to groups of up to12 campers (ages 5-14), sometimes with a co-instructor and sometimes independentlyLead campers in hands-on activities related to the camp themes as well as teambuilding activities, games, and songsEmploy inquiry-based teaching methods to stimulate learningHelp build a sense of community among campers and encourage positive interactions and self-esteem of campersBe a role model for campers by being kind and courteous to all members of the camp community and by being properly prepared for the day’s weather, including wearing the appropriate gearParticipate in, facilitate, and encourage positive, productive interactions between campers, Volunteer Junior Instructors, and fellow interns and staff membersParticipate in camp staff meetings at the beginning and end of each dayCommunicate camper health and behavior concerns with the Camp DirectorDocument accidents and incidents in a timely and appropriate mannerParticipate in working AM and PM extended care coverage on a rotating scheduleEnhance existing curriculum with creative and thought-provoking ideas and activitiesTake initiative in problem-solving, fostering effective interaction between campers, staff, and parentsOther duties as assigned Project Examples:Create signage, social media, or blog posts providing educational interpretation of a natural aspect of our locationCreate signage, social media, or blog posts providing interpretation of a historical aspect of our locationCreate a natural interpretative display for the education center lobbyIdentify, plan, and implement ways to improve trail sustainability (ex/ stepping stones in wet areas)Create and implement a story walk experience on-site for visitorsExpand our community science options for volunteersOther projects available depending on intern’s interests and organization’s needs Work Environment:Activities take place throughout our 160-acre property with over 3 miles of trails through woods and fields. Trail and other program areas may be rocky, wet, muddy, buggy, or sloped. Unless safety is a severe concern (such as thunderstorms), we live by the saying, “There’s no bad weather, only bad gear.”Interns may work with domesticated animals such as chickens, a rabbit, a turtle, and honeybees (direct interaction with the honeybees will be limited to staff with proper training, comfort, and safety gear).Staff will also encounter wild animals which may include insects, snakes, frogs, spiders, salamanders, and native mammals. While Prescott Farm does its best to deter animals in high traffic areas that may cause harm (such as ticks or yellowjackets), as an environmental center, we are not able to predict exactly where these animals will be and avoid taking measures that cause unnecessary harm to our surrounding environment.Dress in accordance with dress code requirements and appropriate for a youth education environment.Interns will receive one-on-one feedback throughout internship and are encouraged to initiate one-on-one conversations with their supervisor as needed. Interns are also encouraged to provide feedback as a means of enhancing the internship program experience.While working at camp, interns should have their cellphones accessible for emergencies but cell phones should be out of sight when campers and their families are present. The camp office and main Prescott Farm office will both be available for staff to use for computer, cell phone, and other internet needs. Qualifications:An individual who is at least 18 years oldAn interest in working with children. Previous camp or teaching experience is desirable but not required.Ability to maintain safety and manage a group of children in a fun and positive way.Must be willing to follow all Prescott Farm health and safety rules.Ability to model responsible behavior to program participants while sharing a sincere interest in the natural and environmental sciences, outdoor skills, and education. Previous experience teaching camp topics is desirable but not required.Ability to function comfortably outdoors in a variety of conditions (cold, hot, rain, humid, buggy, etc.).Creative and collaborative individual able to work independently and as part of a team.Candidate should enjoy working in a busy community, be flexible, highly dependable, and self-motivated.Excellent interpersonal, organizational and leadership skills. Comfort with public speaking, constantly interacting with campers, their families, volunteers, and other staff.First aid and CPR certification recommended but not required.Ability to move program equipment and supplies up to 40 lbs. and navigate nature trails under any weather conditions.Must pass a background check according to NH DHHS rules and Prescott Farm’s guidelines. Benefits:Pay is $16 per hour.Ongoing feedback and development to help staff grow within our organization and in other future pursuits.Opportunities to learn about multiple aspects of nonprofits and environmental education organizations by working closely with all of our staff including environmental educators, preschool staff, volunteer coordinator, marketing director, and administrators.Application:If interested, please go to this website (https://prescottfarm.campbrainstaff.com/), create an account, and fill out the application under “WildQuest Camp Winter & Spring 2027” called “Environmental Education Internship”. If you have any questions, please feel free to reach out to Phoebe Hartvigsen at phartvigsen@prescottfarm.org. We believe our camp community is strengthened by diversity and encourage individuals with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and identities to apply.

jobs.title: Climate Policy Intern at New York State Department of Public Service
jobs.description: Employer: New York State Department of Public Service Expires: 12/09/2026 The New York State Department of Public Service (DPS or Department) works to: ensure safe, affordable, and reliable access to electric, gas, steam, water, and telecommunications services at just and reasonable rates for New York State customers, protect the natural environment, reduce greenhouse gas emissions via transmission and siting of renewable energy resources, and augment the resiliency of utility infrastructure. The Climate Policy Intern will contribute to the development and implementation of clean transportation policies that support New York’s Climate Leadership & Community Protection Act (CLCPA), which adopts the most ambitious climate and clean energy agenda in the country. The CLCPA established aggressive targets to fully transition New York State into a green energy economy and provides a framework to ensure that the transition is equitable and just across all sectors. Interns will work with Department of Public Service (DPS) staff in the evaluation of existing clean transportation policies, as well as the development of future policies and recommendations.The Climate Policy - Clean Energy & Transportation Intern will aid DPS Staff in the evaluation and of development regulatory policy designed to support the equitable implementation of the clean transportation and emissions reductions goals of the CLCPA. Duties Description:The Climate Policy Intern will work in the Office of Markets & Innovation and perform duties that include, but are not limited to:• Conducting in-house research and analysis based on data provided through program administrators.• Assisting in collecting and analyzing data relevant to assessing the achievement of utility program targets and deliverables.• Reviewing and summarizing public comments on relevant proceedings.• Assisting in the analysis of policy implications and identifying potential challenges and opportunities for innovation.• Coordinating the work carried out by consultants and subject matter experts on behalf of the Department.• Coordinating relevant work streams with the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA)• Assisting in the organization of technical conferences and stakeholder feedback sessions.• Helping to maintain current awareness of the Department and stakeholders’ concerns regarding zero emission vehicle programs.• Conducting in-depth research on energy policies, regulations, and market trends to support the achievement of CLCPA targets related to clean transportation and emissions reductions.• Researching best practices from other markets and/or jurisdictions. Minimum Qualifications:• Must be a US citizen or foreign national eligible to work in the United States• Must be 18 years of age or older• Must be currently enrolled in and attending a New York State graduate program, or be a resident of New York State enrolled in and attending a graduate program outside of New York State• Must have a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or equivalent to a C Preferred Skills:• Desire to support New York State’s clean energy sector, including renewable energy, zero emission vehicles, and distributed energy resource technologies.• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with proficiency in reading and interpreting government regulations and legislative texts.• Proficiency in conducting research and literature reviews• Proficiency synthesizing and conveying complex information.• Proficiency in generating actionable insights from data through data preparation, quantitative analysis, and qualitative interpretation.• Proficiency in Microsoft Power BI preferred. Additional Information:Salary: $22.17/hour.Hours: Up to 30 hours per week. Office Location: 3 Empire State Plaza, Albany, New York.Remote Work: A hybrid work schedule may be possible. How to apply: Please send a resume, cover letter, and proof of meeting the minimum qualifications to recruiting@dps.ny.gov or fax to Human Resources Management at (518)473-9990. Please reference “Climate Policy Intern” when applying.

GIS connects data to a map, integrating location data (where things are) with all types of descriptive information (what things are like there). This provides a foundation for mapping and analysis that is used in science and almost every industry. GIS helps users understand patterns, relationships, and geographic context. The benefits include improved communication, efficiency, management, and decision-making. The Iowa DOT utilizes GIS technology from the vendor Esri. The DOT-GIS team is centralized and nature and works closely with many bureaus and teams as well as external partners to lead, guide, and support transportation focused geospatial data management, mapping, and web application development efforts, using GIS technology, that support statewide transportation planning, safety, operations, and data driven decision making.Duties: Contribute and assist with GIS data preparation, clean-up, and quality checks, that lead to map product developmentHelp maintain and publish datasetsSupport enhancements to web based GIS applications and dashboardsSupport data management and data catalog efforts, attend meetings, and participate in cross agency initiatives to improve data consistency, accessibility, and visualization for transportation users.Assist with project specific tasks to be determined upon hire and skills available or training needed, that could include such as updating specific GIS layers or workflows, supporting geospatial analyses, and contributing to enterprise GIS standards efforts. Minimum Qualification Requirements Currently enrolled student in a degree program at an accredited educational institution.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Life Sciences Solutions Market Research at Vizient, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Vizient, Inc. Expires: 12/10/2026 When you’re the best, we’re the best. We instill an environment where employees feel engaged, satisfied and able to contribute their unique skills and talents while living and working as their authentic selves. We provide extensive opportunities for personal and professional development, building both employee competence and organizational capability to fuel exceptional performance through an inclusive environment both now and in the future. Vizient Intern Program Overview: This program is designed to foster a beneficial relationship and provide growth opportunities for Vizient, our employees, and collegiate students. Since 2000, our summer intern program has provided college undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students with practical experience that exposes them to multiple aspects of a career field and the healthcare industry. This full-time, paid intern program offers an opportunity to accelerate academic learning, apply classroom knowledge, and introduce students to a professional setting. Interns are assigned a supervisor to mentor/develop their business skills, as well as monitor their work experiences. Interns are integral members of the company’s team, setting goals, working toward deadlines, and actively participating in community service projects. The program requires the intern to commit to 10 weeks of participation in all formal training, mentoring, on-the-job learning, and opportunities to interact with senior leaders. Program starts June 1, 2027, and ends August 6, 2027 Pay rate: $25 per hour. About the team and role The Life Sciences Market Research team supports pharmaceutical, medical device and healthcare services clients with research and insights that inform business strategy and decision-making. The team conducts qualitative and quantitative research, analyzes market and customer perspectives, and translates findings into clear recommendations for clients and internal stakeholders. The intern will support active market research engagements from project planning through delivery. Working with experienced researchers and consultants, the intern will contribute to research materials, desk research, data organization, interview and survey support, thematic analysis, and presentation development. This role is designed to provide practical exposure to healthcare industry market research while building skills in research execution, analysis and insight communication. What You’ll Do Support market research projects for pharmaceutical, medical device and healthcare services clients. Conduct desk research and organize information from interviews, surveys and secondary sources. Help draft interview guides and surveys, summarize qualitative findings, and perform basic quantitative analysis in Excel. Work with market researchers, consultants and subject-matter experts to support project timelines and deliverables. Prepare clear Excel summaries, charts, presentation slides and written research summaries for internal and client-facing use. Track research tasks, timelines and open questions across multiple projects and contribute ideas to improve research tools and processes. What You’ll Learn Develop an understanding of healthcare markets, including pharmaceutical, medical device and provider perspectives. Build practical experience with qualitative and quantitative market research methods, including interviews, focus groups, surveys, desk research, thematic analysis and basic Excel analysis, as well as PowerPoint storytelling. Learn how researchers and consultants translate customer and market evidence into recommendations for clients. Strengthen organization, written communication, teamwork, project management and presentation skills. Qualifications Currently pursuing an undergraduate degree in market research, marketing, business, healthcare, public health, social science, statistics or a related field. Demonstrated interest in healthcare, life sciences, market research or understanding customer needs. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including organizing data, using formulas and creating basic charts. Coursework or project experience in market research, marketing research, statistics, data analysis or research methods. Familiarity with generative AI tools, such as ChatGPT, for drafting research materials, organizing information and supporting research synthesis. Ability to synthesize information, identify themes and communicate findings clearly in writing and presentations. Preference for candidates who are available to work in Chicago, IL, during the Vizient 2027 Summer Internship Program; other work locations may be considered.

jobs.title: 2027 AKS Development Services Internship Program at AKS Engineering & Forestry LLC
jobs.description: Employer: AKS Engineering & Forestry LLC - AKS Expires: 12/10/2026 Go Beyond the Classroom Looking to build real-world experience this summer? The AKS Internship Program gives college students the chance to apply what they’re learning in the classroom, build practical skills, and contribute in a professional environment. Through meaningful project experience and a supportive team setting, interns gain confidence, broaden their understanding of the industry, and take important steps toward career readiness. How it WorksEach internship experience may look a little different depending on the role and team, but every internship is designed to help students learn by doing. Interns gain hands-on experience through real work, connect with professionals across AKS, and get a better understanding of how different disciplines contribute to project outcomes. For students who return, each summer can build on the last with new experiences, added responsibility, and a deeper understanding of areas that interest them. Students who are interested in returning are encouraged to express interest, and continued participation depends on performance, program fit, and available positions. Interns can expect to work approximately 40-50 hours per week while contributing to project work and day-to-day team priorities. Responsibilities may include: Conducting research and assisting with desktop due diligence related to energy projects, including property ownership, zoning, permitting, utilities, transmission, infrastructure, environmental constraints, and other development considerations. Creating and maintaining project maps, KMZ files, spreadsheets, and other project materials while compiling and organizing information from public databases, agencies, utilities, and other sources. Assisting with project documentation and deliverables, including project summaries, technical memoranda, presentations, meeting materials, action-item tracking, and project files. Pay is provided on an hourly basis, with overtime paid at one and a half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a week. The typical pay range for this position is $19 to $25 per hour. jobs.title: Ambassador at California Environmental Voters
jobs.description: Employer: California Environmental Voters Expires: 12/10/2026 Title: AmbassadorEmployment Type: Part-Time, Non-Exempt (typically 10 to 12 hours per week, with occasional weeks of up to 15)Wage: $20 per hourReports To: Youth Climate Organizing ManagerPosition Location: Central Valley, Sierra Nevada, Sacramento or Inland Empire - HybridWork Schedule: Hybrid schedule – in person at least once every four weeksWHO WE AREWe believe this moment requires transformative change.The climate crisis is here. And Black, Indigenous and people of color have been bearing the burden of our pollution-based economy for generations. We have the solutions to stop climate change, but we lack the political will to do it at the rate and scale that’s needed.EnviroVoters exists to build the political will and power to solve the climate crisis, use climate action to advance justice, and create a global roadmap. To protect our water, land, air, and our most vulnerable communities, we organize voters, elect and train candidates, and hold lawmakers accountable for bold policy change.Our vision is to build resilient, healthy, thriving communities, and create a democracy and economy that is just and sustainable for all.California Environmental Voters (EnviroVoters) and EnviroVoters Education Fund are excited to launch a search for Youth Ambassadors to join our dynamic, fun, and high-performing team!The Ambassadors at EnviroVoters Education Fund are the leaders of the campaign — WE CAN: Water Equity and Clean Air Now! Their campaign tackles the severe inequities surrounding water equity and clean air in the Central Valley, Inland Empire, Sacramento and the Sierra Nevada regions by supporting youth leadership at the forefront of fighting for these issues.The Central Valley, Inland Empire, Sacramento and Sierra Nevada regions have some of the nation’s worst air quality, especially from warehouses, oil production, mining, and agriculture. Long-term health risks like respiratory diseases, lung cancer, and impaired cognitive functioning will severely impact our community if we do not act now.That is why we are calling for all youth aged 18 to 30 to join our team. By joining, you will participate in a nine-month cohort program where together you will learn how to build grassroots power for the environment and climate justice, which includes advocacy for a youth climate board to give young people a voice in local decision-making and community education and outreach to achieve environmental justice for our communities.RESPONSIBILITIESCommit to working an average of 10 to 12 hours per week, with occasional weeks of up to 15 hours during events, retreats, or campaign pushes.Attend weekly online meetings to build skills in grassroots organizing, public speaking, and advocacy, complete administrative tasks, and collaborate with your cohort. Meet in person with your regional cohort at least once a month.Coordinate with your cohort and plan the next phase of the Water Equity and Clean Air Now! Campaign (WE CAN!) to push for youth climate boards in your respective regions. Collaborate with the regional organizers on their campaigns to increase youth engagement in local policy issues.Develop social media content that amplifies local voices, shares success stories, and promotes initiatives that address pressing challenges facing young people and the environment.Develop and lead community initiatives and run grassroots organizing campaigns to advance solutions for community-identified environmental issues and advocate for a vibrant, sustainable, and healthy environment.Foster increased youth participation and leadership in civic processes and actively advocate for policies shaped and led by youth. Support initiatives that cultivate youth leadership and expand opportunities for young people to influence decision-making at all levels.Plan and coordinate events, including but not limited to workshops, informational sessions, volunteer recruitment, and forums aimed at engaging students, youth, community members and to recruit volunteers on issues of clean air and water, and youth civic participation.Expand awareness on climate, environmental policies, environmental justice, and other local issues through digital organizing and social media advocacy. Increase youth civic participation through issue-based organizing and nonpartisan get out the vote activities.Meet with local elected officials and state legislators in their respective regions and in Sacramento to advocate for sustainability initiatives, environmental justice issues, and the importance of youth involvement.Participate and attend the two staff retreats in the Los Angeles and Sacramento areas, one in winter and one in spring.And other duties as assigned.IDEAL CANDIDATE SKILLS The ideal candidate is deeply passionate about protecting the environment and addressing climate change. They have a strong understanding of environmental justice issues and are committed to advocating for equitable solutions. This individual is not only knowledgeable about the issues of climate justice in their community but is also enthusiastic about actively engaging in initiatives that promote equity. They also have the following skills:Ability to commit 10 to 12 hours per week, with flexibility for occasional weeks of up to 15 hours.Passionate about environmental justice, sustainability and environmental policyStrong communication, social, and interpersonal skills, with an aptitude for inspiring and mobilizing others.Experience in community engagement, youth empowerment, and leadership development.Strong public speaking skillsGood time management Critical thinking skillsAttention to detail Self-motivated and willing to take initiativeAbility to work autonomously and as part of a teamWHAT ELSE YOU SHOULD KNOWThis is an outstanding opportunity for a highly motivated candidate to assume a pivotal role with this highly respected organization from January 2027 – September 2027.There are opportunities to extend the role into a two-year program following the conclusion of this term.While the role is mostly conducted remotely, you should be based in California’s Central Valley, Sacramento, Sierra Nevada region, or the Inland Empire.California Environmental Voters and the California Environmental Voters Education Fund are committed to workplace diversity and inclusion. We are equal opportunity employers and do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy (including childbirth, breastfeeding, and related medical conditions), reproductive health decision making, marital status, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. California Environmental Voters and the California Environmental Voters Education Fund have a deep commitment to equity and fostering a culture of inclusion. We invite and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including those from groups traditionally underrepresented in employment, who may contribute to further diversifying our organization. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact HR@envirovoters.org.
